newsitem.title: LATVIA: SHARE SALE OVERSHADOWS UNIBANKA RESULT.
newsitem.headline: SHARE SALE OVERSHADOWS UNIBANKA RESULT.

text.p: Latvia's market was expected to shrug off Unibanka's six-month results and focus on a July 28 auction of one million of the state's shares in the bank, brokers said on Tuesday.
The Riga stock exchange said on Tuesday the bank's first half profit was 3.185 million lats compared to 3.6 million lats for the same period last year.
"Unibanka's net profit was very good and better than expected, as it only reported a 1.4 million lat profit for the first quarter," Harijs Zulgis, chief broker at Rigas komercbanka, told Reuters.
"But the auction will have a bigger impact on the share price, at least in the short-term," he said.
The Latvian Privatisation Agency said last week it would auction one million of the state's shares in the bank at no less than 3.05 lats per share.
The announcement has pulled the bank's price down for three straight sessions. It fell Tuesday to 3.10 lats from 3.15 lats.
"Unibanka's price should stabilise at around 3.05 lats," Zulgis said.
His comments were echoed by other dealers, who saw the auction and the uncertainty about a future sale of a similiar block of shares weighing on the share price.
"If it wasn't for this sale, which took a lot of people by surprise, it could have reached 3.50 lats and stayed there," said one dealer.
"A lot of the buyers who invested in Unibanka before did not expect the privatisation agency to sell such a large block and there is a fear they could do it again," the dealer added.
"It's very curious that the privatisation agency wants to sell so many shares at such a low price," said Artis Goba, a broker at Saules Banka.
He added that Unibanka's six-month result would probably not have had much impact on its price even without the auction.
"It's result is not much different from what it was last year and its 1997 profit forecast is about the same," he said.
"But its capital is up, so its earning per share look down a bit this year," he added.
